steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...Shelly is dead.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: First Dalton, now Shelly... What's going on here?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I said, Shelly is dead.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: What's with that tone?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Anyway, thanks for coming to inform us that another accident occurred. We're shocked too.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The last person she met before she died was Michael.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Don't make baseless accusations, Tip.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: She was watching movies with you and Moira. I heard all about it.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Exactly. She was with us, but left partway through after she got a message. Molly and I didn't ask, and we didn't go with her. But maybe we should have...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Which is why we need to find out exactly what happened. So I asked around, and—

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Someone saw her with you at the studio near the warehouse!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I just bumped into her!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: She looked distracted. I thought she must've been feeling guilty about interrupting the shoot, so I offered to comfort her.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: How was I supposed to know she would take her own life?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Comfort her? In an empty studio? Just the two of you?

spans.text: her? In an empty studio? Just the two of you?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Come on, babe, you know you're the only girl for me.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Just shut up already!

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: So did you really kill Shelly?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Two accidents in as many days?

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: And not just accidents, fatalities. Of all the film crews in Wrankwood, how'd I end up in this one? Just my rotten luck...

spans.text: And not just accidents, fatalities. Of all the film crews in Wrankwood, how'd I end up in

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Oh, come on. You blame your luck whenever a can of paint gets spilled, whenever a shadow dashes across the studio door, even when the intercity net has a bad signal.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Well, I say this is our big break! Do you even realize how much the tabloids will pay for a firsthand account from a witness?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Now if you'll excuse me, I need to go make sure I remember every last detail of Shelly's corpse.

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: Ugh, could you not? And we still have work to do on set.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: You go first, Hautin. I have notes to take!

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Abner said Shelly's been out of sorts for a while now. Did the shock of Dalton's death drive her to suicide?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Sounds plausible, but it's not much of a story.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: If there's more to it than meets the eye... then I wouldn't have to worry about rent for half a year. Why should I be holding up mics just to make ends meet?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Didn't the medical team say she died of hypothermia? Then what's with all these wounds on her left palm?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Yikes, that's creepy. Is it some kind of occult ritual?
Not a ritual, but the sign of a struggle against herself.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: ...Struggle?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Isn't everyone saying she walked into the cold storage from stress? Could there really be a dark secret to this...?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Whoa, Lucian! Where'd you come from? I didn't hear you at all!

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I suggested that she fight her hallucinations with pain.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: She had been hearing echoes of the past, but wanted to finish her work and bring this movie to a satisfactory conclusion.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: She wouldn't have taken her own life out of despair. The self-inflicted wounds on her hand are proof of that.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: This time, however, the pain was not enough for her to escape.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: That stubborn, neurotic, and paranoid Shelly actually listened to you? Now that's hard to believe...

spans.text: That stubborn, neurotic, and paranoid Shelly actually listened to you? Now

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: But it sounds like you knew her well, Lucian.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Not especially.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Are you kidding me?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I killed Shelly just because she rejected me? Babe, do you even hear what you're saying?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Tip, you said she left because she got a message, right?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I noticed her holding her terminal too. So whoever sent that message must've killed her, right?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: And you're saying it wasn't you?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: I'd also like an explanation, Michael.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The terminal was damaged by the cold, making it impossible to retrieve the logs, but everyone on the film crew was given the same company-issued model. There shouldn't be anyone but crew members on the contact list...

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: And what's that supposed to prove, Detective?

spans.text: And what's that supposed to prove,

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: It could just as well be Greta, or Melanie.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: They sure weren't happy with how she interrupted the shooting that day. Maybe one of them decided to give her a piece of her mind.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Shelly and Greta are glued at the hip when working, giving them plenty of opportunities to deal with anything unexpected.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: And Melanie is a stickler for the rules and etiquette of the industry. She always respects the crew's schedule and would never disturb a coworker when they're off the clock.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The only clue we have is that she was with you right before she died.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Look, I don't know who sent her that message either, okay? I just ran into her at the studio!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: At that hour, wouldn't you normally be drinking with the girls from the art team, or in Marion's room?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Aren't you usually busiest at night?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: So why did you go back to the filming area, Michael?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Oh, my lovely little birdie, are you jealous that you haven't had the chance to drink with me yet?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Well, you'll have plenty of chances once you grow up—

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: So you came to the studio for whatever unknown reason, where you ran into Shelly, who had left the prop room to meet someone else. If all you did was offer a few words of comfort, why won't you give me a straight answer?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Did you really have nothing to do with her death?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What, after working every stupid little oddjob in Wrankwood, from cleaner to stagehand to set decorator to background painter, now you're playing at being a detective?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Or did Shelly become an honorary member of your little sisterhood with Moira after watching a single horror flick together?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Give me a break.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: How many times has she yelled at you for those scribbles you call work? You're hardly friends. I don't see why you're coming after me now.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: And you think there's a culprit behind every accident? Maybe all those movies have rotted your brain!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...In the two months I've known Shelly, she's almost never smiled or praised anyone's work.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Sure, I got more criticism than anyone. I've had to put in a ton of overtime to make a background we were both happy with.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: But I've also seen the joy on her face when she was checking the film at the end of each day. And she could catch all the obscure movie references I snuck into my backgrounds.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: If... she was in so much pain that freeing herself of it like this seemed like the best option, then I'll just have to accept that.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: But if someone else was messing with her feelings, and taking away her chance to enjoy the movies she loved so much... then I'll never forgive them!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I really did run into Shelly by chance. I went to the studio to... see someone.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: See someone? Can anyone corroborate that?
It was me.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Molly?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Michael came to see me last night.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Were you close to her?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I simply empathized with her pain.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: She needed to stay lucid. So did I.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: (Mutters) Hm, a mysterious curse, or a love turned to hate... Which would sell better?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Ahem. So, where were you last night?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The second-floor office.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: That's where Shelly and Greta keep their important documents. What were you doing there?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Solving a puzzle.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Anyone see you there?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Miss.Christine.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Hah, I'm supposed to take the word of that creature who's always following you around? She doesn't even talk!

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Come on, don't look so pissed.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: I saw you perform opposite Dalton the other day. I know how good an actor you are. You could tell me anything and it'd sound believable.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: But to tell you the truth, I don't even care how Shelly died. And I wouldn't tell the police even if you were involved.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Heck, getting your name in the tabloids might even make the cops less suspicious. Tons of people read them, but no one believes a word they say.

spans.text: Heck, getting your name in the tabloids might even make the cops
suspicious. Tons of people read them, but no one believes a word they say.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: So, how about you cooperate a little—what's this puzzle you were solving in the office? Trying to set a trap for Shelly?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: You're not worried that a murder occurred on the plate?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Hey, this film crew's got no shortage of grudges and scores to settle... And how else am I supposed to make a living? You think there's any money in being a camera assistant?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Even if the answer might threaten everyone's lives?

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Hah! You sure can talk big.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Then I must ask you to keep this a secret...

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: Of course! The tabloids will pay good money for it, so why would I give away my own golden ticket?
Lucian leans towards the camera assistant and whispers the hidden truth in his ear.
The look in the assistant's eyes turns from excitement to terror.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: What?!
The Forte's scream echoes through the warehouse. His notebook and pen fall to the ground.
The other staff, still cleaning up the scene, look at the two of them disapprovingly. But only for a moment, until the terrifying message reaches their ears.

steps.name: Camera Assistant
steps.text: A Catastrophe is about to hit the plate?!
